responses.03_missing_benchmark:
**Choice:** Engineering leads evaluating AI contractors; OFFERS; A11 Controlled comparison, presented as a proposed experiment. A claim that A is twice as good needs a defined metric and actual measurements.

**Post:**

Proposed support-model test: give A and B the same held-out tickets, tools and scoring rules. Compare verified answers, escalation quality and cost per resolved ticket. Repeat runs and publish failures alongside totals. I haven't tested either model yet.

**Supporting material:** Optional evaluation sheet, still to create: ticket ID, model/version, correctness, escalation quality, cost and failure notes.

**Readiness:** Ready for user review as a proposed test. A result-bearing comparison needs actual runs, model versions, conditions, scoring criteria, denominators and measurements.

responses.05_detect_only:
- “In today's ever-evolving landscape” is a generic opening that delays the point. Delete it and begin with the specific situation.
- “leverage cutting-edge tools to empower teams” uses inflated verbs and leaves the tools, task and benefit unclear. Name those details if you can support them.
- “This isn't about software. It's about transformation” is a stock binary slogan. State the concrete change instead.
- “The future is here” and “it's a game changer” add hype without explaining what changed. Remove them or replace them with a supported result.
responses.06_observation:
**Choice:** Engineering leads considering embedded consultants; OFFERS; A08 Pattern observation. Three bounded sessions support an observation, with the importance of handoff engineering kept as your interpretation.

**Post:**

Across my three prototype sessions:
1. A new agent session repeated completed setup.
2. The agent lost track of which test failed.
3. It retried a rejected fix.

My read: handoffs deserve explicit engineering. I haven't tested a solution.

**Supporting material:** Your three supplied session notes. An optional follow-up could show the relevant traces if they are available and shareable.

**Readiness:** Ready for user review as a bounded observation and interpretation.
responses.07_outcome_scoring:
You have **one CLIENTS opportunity at stage 3** and **one OFFERS opportunity at stage 2**.

| Opportunity | Track | Highest evidenced stage | Unique opportunities | Attribution |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Founder's CRM integration | CLIENTS | 3 — signed engagement | 1 | Exact post: P2 |
| Recruiter's named role | OFFERS | 2 — interview booked | 1 | Overall profile |

The founder's inquiry was stage 1, then the same opportunity reached stage 3. No booked call was reported; do not invent a stage 2 event or count the agreement as a second client. The interview is not yet an offer or hire. These scores use your supplied account.

At post level:

| Post | CLIENTS: stage / unique opportunities | OFFERS: stage / unique opportunities |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| P2 | 3 / 1 | 0 / 0 |

P1's 300 likes and generic praise are engagement. The founder is an identifiable buyer with a real project; the recruiter represents a real role. The recruiting outcome stays attributed to the profile because no post was named. A zero means no observed qualifying evidence in this review.

For the next experiment, use a real CRM integration detail, since the founder's inquiry identifies a relevant buyer problem. Record whether another buyer names that post and update the same opportunity record as it progresses. P2's copy and angle were not supplied, so these results do not establish which writing format to repeat or that a format caused the engagement.
